_about: A bank of styles to mix, layer by layer, like an alchemist. Krish, 2026-10-14: "I don't think that these things are just one way of everything being in the future. I think we need to build a bank of different styles that we know can be modularized and used. You already have a tonne of pre-existing knowledge of what I like and, more importantly, what I don't like, which you can lean on and I don't think should be totally overwritten. I would prefer to build a modular bank of styles over time that we can draw inspiration from and mix together at different layers, like an alchemist." The base always applies and is never overwritten by a module; a module is mixed into one piece's recipe, and Krish's verdict after the piece says whether it stays in the bank as liked, untested or not for us.

base.about: What Krish already likes and, more importantly, does not like. Every recipe sits on top of this; where a module disagrees with the base, the base wins unless Krish says otherwise for that piece.

references.krish_likes: I generally love how she talks about complex topics observationally. She's not commentating on a specific thing or company but she's just unpacking how something works that people probably don't even realise they wondered about. I think the same is going to happen in AI and we could do a really good job of talking less about companies and more about concepts.

bank.name: Concede, then claim
bank.how: Grant the reasonable view first, then make the sharp claim inside 15 seconds.
bank.fits: concept pieces and arguments against a popular view

bank.name: One person, one situation
bank.how: Explain the system through one ordinary person in one moment, then widen to everyone.

bank.name: The image that names it
bank.how: One everyday metaphor that names how it works ("a market becomes a queue").

bank.name: One number, after the story
bank.how: A single hard number as proof, placed after the story so it lands.
bank.fits: any piece with one strong figure

bank.name: The better way, briefly
bank.how: Show the alternative in two lines before the close.

bank.name: A wry close
bank.how: End on an observation that makes them smile, not a lecture.

bank.name: Thinking out loud
bank.how: Asides ("by the way", "right?"), self-aware humour, a person thinking, not presenting.

bank.name: Long holds with punch-ins
bank.how: Few cuts (about 3 a minute); step in inside the take on key lines.

bank.name: Simple flat illustrations
bank.how: Plain illustrated scenes only where the story needs a picture, about a fifth of the runtime.

bank.name: Cut on every phrase
bank.how: About 33 cuts a minute, shots around a second.

bank.name: The number in the scene
bank.how: The key number as a big graphic laid into the picture, not a caption.
bank.fits: any piece with one money or scale number

bank.name: Words inside the picture
bank.how: Key words placed in the scene (on a wall, a table) instead of a caption strip.

bank.name: Ask for a send
bank.how: End with "send this to someone who ..." instead of "tell me in the comments".

bank.name: Wide handheld first-person
bank.how: Wide-angle, moving, first-person shots.
bank.fits: b-roll from a place or an event

bank.name: The face fills the frame
bank.how: No split screen: the speaker fills the tall frame, close, with a warm key light and a coloured rim light; pictures cut in full-screen instead of sharing the frame.
bank.fits: the 90-second cut first; the long cut once tested

bank.name: Captions as typography
bank.how: Two to four words at a time, centred low over the chest, never a subtitle bar: a light geometric sans for most words, the word that carries the meaning in bold, and the payoff phrase in a large italic serif with a warm gradient and a soft glow.
bank.note: Needs faces outside the brand set (Anton, Archivo, IBM Plex Mono): a light sans and an italic serif. Krish asked to upgrade the typography (17 Oct); the faces themselves are his to approve.

bank.name: One object on a dark, grainy card
bank.how: A full-screen cutaway: a dark charcoal-to-slate gradient with film grain, a two-word line at the top ("but now", light then bold) and one large real object in the middle, lit and glowing (a company's real logo tile, a real product screen).
bank.fits: the turn of an argument, a company or product entering the story
bank.note: The crown on the Claude logo is a playful prop, not an analogy acted out; any prop still passes ANALOGY_IN_SCRIPTS_ONLY (no car, gear or race standing for an AI).

bank.name: Numbered levels as chapters
bank.how: The piece promised as a count ("in 10 levels") and each chapter a full-screen card: the number in a bold italic serif ("Level 3") over a short plain line in a light sans ("is power").
bank.fits: long episodes with chapters; explainers that build step by step

bank.name: Negative-film illustration
bank.how: An illustration in inverted, negative-film tones on the dark card, under the chapter title.
bank.fits: chapter cards, when a real screenshot cannot show the idea
bank.note: Only where it shows a real thing: a picture acting out an analogy is out (ANALOGY_IN_SCRIPTS_ONLY).

bank.name: Every word bounces in
bank.how: Each caption word arrives on the frame it is said with a quick overshoot (scale up a touch past full, settle) and a fade; the group holds, then clears for the next.
bank.from: Jack Roberts Story ad, 17 Oct (Krish: "These words all bounce in")

bank.name: Something is always moving
bank.how: No still frame: a slow push on the speaker within every shot, cards that drift and scale while they hold, words animating in; a cut or a move every couple of seconds.
bank.from: Jack Roberts Story ad, 17 Oct (Krish: "there's a lot more movement on the screen")
bank.fits: the 90-second cut; the long cut at a calmer rate

bank.name: The room behind him is treated
bank.how: The speaker is cut from the room (a person mask, feathered and steady from frame to frame) and the room is softened, darkened and graded towards the brand's ink, with a vignette, so it reads as a set, not a spare room.
bank.from: Jack Roberts Story ad, 17 Oct (Krish: "The background of the person has also been treated when he's talking so it doesn't look too amateur")
